prompt: How many frames does the video stream of returns.mp4 hold?
What does the MP4 container itself add for a model to read?

choices.text: The subtitles of the video
choices.why: Subtitles would be a stream inside it, and this file has none.

choices.text: A summary of the content
choices.why: No container summarises anything.

choices.text: Nothing a model reads
choices.why: Right. It holds the streams together and in time; the model reads frames or sound, never the box they came in.

choices.text: A description of every keyframe
choices.why: Keyframes are pictures in the video stream, not descriptions.

prompt: Why is asking a decoder for frame 300 slower than it looks?

choices.text: Frame 300 has to be downloaded again
choices.why: The file is local; the work is decoding.

choices.text: Every frame is a full picture and they are large
choices.why: Most frames are differences, which is why the file is small.

choices.text: The audio has to be decoded first
choices.why: The streams are decoded separately.

choices.text: It rebuilds it from the last keyframe
choices.why: Right, applying every difference after it: most frames are stored as changes from the one before.

prompt: What joins what was shown to what was said?

choices.text: The clock that the two streams share
choices.why: Right. Timestamps in seconds from the start.

choices.text: The order of the frames in the file
choices.why: Order alone does not say which words go with which frame.

choices.text: The scene detector
choices.why: It finds cuts; the clock is what lines them up with speech.

choices.text: The H.264 codec
choices.why: It compresses the pictures and knows nothing of speech.

prompt: Why did a frame every second miss the card?

choices.text: The card was too dark for OCR
choices.why: Scene detection saw it and OCR read it.

choices.text: ffmpeg handed over a later frame for the tick at 21
choices.why: Right. Frames from 20.5 to 21.5 round to that tick and the filter keeps the last, from the next slide.

choices.text: ffmpeg skips frames with no sound
choices.why: The fps filter knows nothing about sound.

choices.text: One frame a second is too many to read
choices.why: All 33 were read; none was the card.

prompt: How many frames did the threshold of 0.03 pick out?
Why did a scene threshold of 0.3 find only two frames?

choices.text: The video has only two scenes
choices.why: It has seven slides.

choices.text: Slide changes scored far lower
choices.why: Right, about 0.04 to 0.06. Only the cuts into and out of the dark card scored 1.0.

choices.text: The detector stops after two frames
choices.why: It runs over the whole video.

choices.text: Keyframes were missing
choices.why: Scene detection does not use keyframes.

prompt: The 0.03 scene detector saw six titles, not seven. Which one did it miss, and why?

choices.text: The card, because it is too short
choices.why: It saw the card; that is its strength.

choices.text: The refund slide, because it is the last
choices.why: There is a cut into it at 26.44.

choices.text: Slide 3, whose change was too small
choices.why: That is what the keyframes missed, not 0.03.

choices.text: The first slide, which no cut leads into
choices.why: Right. The timeline adds the first frame by hand.

prompt: Match each frame rule to where it is weak.
Why does each piece of the transcript have a start and an end?

choices.text: Whisper prints a start and an end for every word it hears
choices.why: The times come from cutting at silences first.

choices.text: Each silence-bounded stretch was transcribed alone
choices.why: Right. Silero VAD found the stretches.

choices.text: The MP4 container stores the times beside the audio
choices.why: This file has no subtitle stream.

choices.text: The slides mark when each sentence starts
choices.why: Slides and speech are separate streams.

prompt: Why is "Fourth," missing from the transcript of step four?

choices.text: The narrator did not say it in the recording

choices.text: Whisper does not know the word Fourth
choices.why: It wrote First, Second and Third.

choices.text: The card covered it

choices.text: The segment began after the word
choices.why: Right. A word clipped at a segment boundary.

prompt: In timeline.py, which scene does a piece of speech belong to?

choices.text: The scene it starts in
choices.why: The program uses the middle.

choices.text: The scene its middle falls in
choices.why: Right. A simple rule, and it says so.

choices.text: The scene with the most similar title
choices.why: No text comparison is made.

choices.text: Every scene it overlaps
choices.why: Each piece goes to exactly one scene.

prompt: What does the timeline do with the OCR's RETURN3O?

choices.text: Corrects it to RETURN30
choices.why: A timeline does not correct its sources.

choices.text: Drops it, because OCR was unsure
choices.why: No confidence was checked; it is kept.

choices.text: Keeps it where it was
choices.why: Right, beside its time and the other stream. An error kept in place is checked at its second.

choices.text: Moves it to the speech column
choices.why: It was shown, not said.

prompt: Which piece of information is only in the speech, not on any slide?

choices.text: Code: RETURN30
choices.why: Shown and never said.

choices.text: Within 30 days of delivery
choices.why: That is on the refund slide.

choices.text: Where refunds go
choices.why: Right: back to the card you paid with. A pipeline that only looks would lose it.

prompt: How many tokens is the timeline as text, by o200k_base?
By the tile rule, how many tokens is one 1280 by 720 frame at high detail?
For a video of slides and speech, why is the timeline the right thing to send?

choices.text: Because models cannot read video frames
choices.why: They can; it costs much more.

choices.text: Because it is shorter than the soundtrack
choices.why: Length of audio is not the comparison here.

choices.text: Because OCR is more accurate than a vision model
choices.why: OCR made a mistake here too; the point is cost for what matters.

choices.text: It is far cheaper and keeps the slides' text

prompt: The course's illustrative summary says RETURN30 with a zero, though OCR read RETURN3O. What is the lesson's point about that?

choices.text: The summary is wrong and should say RETURN3O

choices.text: OCR should be replaced by a VLM

choices.text: Silent corrections will one day be wrong

prompt: For a video you know nothing about, what is the lesson's safe default for picking frames?

choices.text: Scene detection at 0.03
choices.why: 0.03 was tuned for this video and is wrong for most.

choices.text: Keyframes, because they are free
choices.why: Fine as a first pass; chosen for compression.

choices.text: A fixed rate plus scene changes
choices.why: Right: the rate for coverage, scene changes for cuts. Each covers the other's blind spot.

choices.text: Every frame, to be safe
choices.why: 900,575 tokens for 32 seconds.

prompt: At one frame a second and 1,105 tokens each, how many tokens is an hour of video?
Put the steps for long video in the order the lesson gives them.
items: keep a frame per scene at low detail

prompt: A shop's product videos are long single shots: a hand turning a book slowly to show its condition. Which frame rule fits?

choices.text: A fixed rate
choices.why: Right. Continuous change with no cuts is what a fixed rate covers.

choices.text: Scene detection, tuned low
choices.why: There are no cuts, and a gradual change is scene detection's blind spot.

choices.text: Keyframes only
choices.why: The encoder places them for compression, and a slow turn may get few.

choices.text: The soundtrack alone
choices.why: The condition of the book is visual.

prompt: A summary of a training video says "the form must be signed in blue ink". The timeline has no entry that says so. What do you do?

choices.text: Keep it; models notice details people miss
choices.why: Nothing the model read says it. It came from no source.

choices.text: Treat it as unsupported
choices.why: Right, until a moment in the video shows it. Every claim should point at an entry; this one points nowhere.

choices.text: Re-run the summary until it disappears
choices.why: That hides the problem; it does not check the claim.

choices.text: Add more frames at high detail and trust the next summary
choices.why: More input does not verify a claim; checking it against the video does.
